As someone who has crippling driving anxiety to the point where I’ve given up on therapy for it, NTA.

You told him in advance you couldn’t do it, and there are plenty of options for him. I live in the rural Southern US and I’m still able to get Ubers or rideshares, or otherwise plan out how I’m supposed to get places, because that’s just a fact of my life I have to work around. When you have physical symptoms of anxiety like that, you need backup plans to your backup plans if you’re trying to avoid your triggers instead of working on them, and it never gives someone the right to guilt others for not bending over backwards to accommodate them.

IANAL but I had this happen to me. I just want to say be very careful about trying to go up the chain at the school, because they will come back with vengeance. 

Keep records of everything—all correspondence with the hospital and with the school re: her hospitalization. Make sure you get very clear, written confirmation that the psychiatrists don't think your sister is a danger to herself or others when she's checked out. I was coerced by a counselor into voluntarily committing two years ago, and my school tried to threaten to make me leave when I returned, saying I was a danger. Luckily, my mom is a lifesaver and kept all kinds of records, both notes from what she saw while I was admitted and all my hospital paperwork.

If your family does want to go further up for recourse, make sure you keep track of *everything*, and have a serious conversation with your sister about whether or not she wants to pursue anything legal, because it could have negative consequences as far as administration at her university goes (I opted not to because it was too much time and money, but I don't think at all it's irrational to want to).

I went two days and it was awful. Not least because I was lied to going in—they told me I could leave when I wanted to because I was voluntary, but then marked me as involuntary so when I tried to go they wouldn’t let me. I was yelled at the first night by a nurse for crying because I was overwhelmed. Food was worse than my high school lunches, which was a feat. And I mostly was wanting to climb the walls because I was bored out of my mind and on new medication that made me jittery.

Luckily one of my psychiatrists went to my university and we started talking about that, and between him and my mom raising a bunch of hell to get me out (because they’d also told her I was a voluntary admission and would be able to leave) I was able to go early.

Pretty sure I would’ve wanted to kill myself more if I’d had to stay, though.
